title: multi-mode-deployment-safety-layers-canary-ab-shadow-autorestore
creator: Ava Martinez
description:
Goal: Build a reusable 'safety layers' subsystem that translates a single rollout intent (canary / A/B / shadow / auto-rollback) into environment-specific execution for Hosted, Dedicated, and Private deployments. Problem: Our current rollout controller assumes hosted networking and infra primitives. Dedicated pools and Private (VPC / on-prem) have different constraints (no external sidecars, restricted egress, private KMS, different autoscaling semantics), leading to ad-hoc work and drift. This ticket scopes design + prototype + tests for a controller that emits environment adapters, policy validators, and environment-aware canary analysis.

Key outcomes:
- One declarative rollout DSL (percentage, metrics, epoch, synthetic traffic) that compiles to environment-targeted plans.
- Safe default thresholds and auto-rollback rules tuned per environment class.
- Shadowing implementation that works in-hosted edge, dedicated pool proxies, and on-prem network mirrors (via local bridge).
- Observable, consistent canary signals (latency P50/P95, error-rate, token-cost delta, U-test quality regression) reported to Console with per-env metadata.

Why now: Increased Dedicated and Private onboarding requests; risk of regressions during cross-mode promotions; customers require traceable, auditable rollouts with environment constraints respected.
acceptance_criteria: A single rollout manifest can be submitted to the control plane and will be executed in Hosted, Dedicated, and Private without manual manifest edits
Environment adapters enforce environment constraints (no external egress for Private, KMS key usage, tenant isolation) before rollout starts
Canary analysis produces the same metric set in Console with environment tag and supports auto-rollback when thresholds are breached
Shadow traffic implemented for all three modes: hosted-edge mirror, dedicated pool proxy mirror, and private-bridge mirror (local process or VPN)
End-to-end test harness that simulates a canary that fails metrics and triggers an automatic rollback; test results stored in CI and a dashboard visible to SRE/PM
Security review completed and private deployment flows validated with KMS/HSM and no plaintext model artifacts leaked
tasks: Design: rollout DSL + environment adapter spec (owner: Kai) — 2 days
Prototype: compiler that emits per-env plan (hosted/dedicated/private) — 5 days
Implement: adapter hooks in runtime controller + policy validators — 6 days
Shadow bridge: implement lightweight mirror for private networks + e2e tests — 5 days
Telemetry: add environment tags to canary metrics and Console UI section — 4 days
CI: add simulated failing canary test, auto-rollback validation — 3 days
Security: run KMS/HSM integration checklist and threat model review — 2 days
Docs: rollout runbook and onboarding checklist for Dedicated/Private customers — 2 days

notes:
Trade-offs considered:
- Option A: keep separate controllers per environment (fast but divergent).
- Option B: single controller with adapters (more upfront work, better long-term parity).
Decision: implement single controller + pluggable adapters to avoid config drift.

Auto-rollback heuristics (proposal):
- Primary signals: error-rate increase > 0.5% absolute or 3x relative, latency P95 regression > 30% baseline, token-cost per request > 20% increase, or significant quality regression measured by a weighted prompt-set U-test (p<0.05).
- Per-environment multipliers: Hosted: strict default thresholds; Dedicated: slightly relaxed pct thresholds if customer has reserved capacity; Private: strict safety on egress/keys but metrics thresholds aligned with hosted once telemetry validated.

Implementation notes:
- Shadowing in Private uses local bridge that writes sanitized request metadata to a local queue; an optional secure forwarder can ship aggregated metrics to Redwood if customer consents.
- For Dedicated, mirror traffic at the pool-proxy layer; ensure we respect tenant isolation and do not contest resources for live traffic.
- Compiler will reject rollouts that require features not available in the target environment (example: VPC private install with no mirror configured and policy requires shadowing).
